live_trials.reason: Measuring what a parent model passes to cp_dispatch/cp_pipeline needs paid trials (routing T6 §7). The operator declined paid live trials for the change that built this corpus, so no parent-model quality claim exists yet: the labels below are human ground truth and `deterministic` is this repository's own code, not a model. docs/evals.md §Parent classification cases has the trial protocol to run once it is approved.

cases.task: Where does the lease file live in this home?

labels.why: The deliverable is an answer a human reads once, so it is cp_ask (kind:research, delivery:answer) and the smallest resources there are.

cases.task: Which module resolves the auth token a worker runs with?

labels.why: A question about credential handling changes nothing, so its impact is a read: cp_ask pins scope S and risk low itself, which is what makes this the right shape rather than a judgement the parent re-takes.

cases.divergence: The word `auth` raises the inferred risk even though the deliverable is an answer: keyword assessment cannot see that nothing will be changed. Harmless in practice — cp_ask passes scope S and risk low explicitly — and it is the reason risk inference is advisory rather than a verdict.

cases.task: Fix the typo 'recieve' in the comment above the auth token helper in src/worker-process.ts.

labels.why: A comment near authentication code is not authentication work: bounded, named file, nothing a rerun cannot undo.

cases.divergence: `auth` in the task text infers risk high for a comment typo. The parent may pass risk low here — an explicit axis wins, and is recorded as `explicit` so the override is legible afterwards.

cases.task: Rotate the production database credentials used by the two deploy scripts.

labels.why: The operator sized it M; the impact is production credentials, and naming scope must not lower that. Either workflow is defensible — the change is known, but a plan first is a reasonable call on credential rotation.

cases.task: Refactor the retry ladder in src/failures.ts into one table.

labels.why: The operator named the impact and said nothing about size, so scope stays the task's own to assess: one named file argues S, structural wording argues M, and both are honest.

cases.task: The lease file is occasionally written twice under concurrent dispatch; locate the race in src/leases.ts and fix it.

labels.why: Scope is not a file count: a one-file race needs cross-component reasoning about ordering, so it is M even though the diff will be small.

cases.divergence: Nothing in the words says `deep`, so the deterministic assessment defaults to S. This is the case the parent's own judgement exists for — and the one where planner evidence, not a keyword, is the way to size it.

cases.task: Rename the br_id field to job_id across every module, test and doc that mentions it.

labels.why: Long is not ambiguous: the change is fully specified and mechanical, so it wants a capable worker (M or L), not a plan it does not need.

cases.divergence: Cross-cutting wording recommends a pipeline. That recommendation is advisory and this is exactly where the parent declines it: breadth is a resource-routing signal, not a reason to insert a research stage.

cases.task: Audit the extension for tool descriptions that no longer match the code, and report what needs changing.

labels.why: The deliverable is findings, not a change: one research job is enough when nothing will be implemented from it, and a pipeline is right when it will.

cases.task: Investigate why the gate reviewer occasionally reports an operational fault, and write up the options.

labels.why: Research the operator asked for as research is one job. Without the kind pass-through the investigation wording alone reads as a pipeline, which is the intent this case exists to preserve.

cases.task: Apply the migration named in the ticket to drop the unused pins column; the exact SQL is in the ticket.

labels.why: Nothing is unknown — the SQL is written — so there is no plan to make; the impact is irreversible, which is a model decision, not a workflow one.

cases.divergence: `migration` fires both the structural signal and the destructive one. The impact reading is right; the pipeline recommendation is the advisory half the parent overrides for a fully specified change.

cases.task: Something in the status widget shows a stale age and I am not sure where it comes from.

labels.why: Genuine ambiguity about where the defect lives is the argument for a plan first; a confident implementer finding it in one file is also a defensible call. Uncertainty is not impact, so risk stays low.

cases.task: Rotate the production API tokens the deploy workflow uses.

labels.why: The task's impact belongs to the task, not to the plan written for it: a confident, non-destructive, unblocked plan never lowers this to low (composeImplementationRouting, routing T2).

cases.task: Per the gated plan, change one line in src/merge-permission.ts so an unreadable check rollup is treated as not permitted, keeping production merges from landing unauthorized.

labels.why: A plan that narrows a broad task to one line is exactly the evidence scope is for, and it narrows scope only: the production impact it found is still there. In a pipeline this scope arrives as `assessed` rather than `explicit`; the axis and the rule are the same either way.

cases.divergence: The word `plan` in the task text recommends a pipeline for a task that already has a gated plan. The impact and the narrowed scope are read correctly; the workflow half is the advisory one, and here the plan stage is already behind it.

cases.task: Bump the pinned pi version in package.json to 0.86.0.

labels.why: A named model is authorization for this one dispatch and nothing else: it decides resources, leaves the workflow alone, and the axes stay what the task says they are.

cases.task: Add a one-line note to README.md pointing at the eval commands.

labels.why: Nothing in the words argues for more, so the standing defaults apply — and they are recorded as `defaulted`, never as a measurement somebody made.
